author: Primal Space
description:
Before BIC Cristal’s launch in 1950, pens were a luxury item, retailing at around $150 – a price completely out of reach for most ordinary people. But Marcel Bich’s design absolutely changed the game.

Taking inspiration from an earlier design by László Bíró, he utilized state-of-the-art Swiss watchmaking machines to mass-produce stainless steel balls, and opted for a simple, clear plastic barrel to produce a pen that could be sold for just $2.

All he needed to do now was drop the ‘H’ from his name, and one of the most iconic global brands was born!

It’s not just Bich’s design that’s impressive. Perhaps his real legacy should be the impact his pen had on literacy rates. In the decades after the BIC Cristal was introduced, literacy rose from 33% to an incredible 90%. Not bad for an ‘ordinary’ pen!
title: These Pens Increased Literary Rates
